statement: One retention owner for terminal replica_operations and storage_reservations rows. It retires a row only when the row is terminal, past its horizon and proven unreferenced, with one referenced-predicate per dependency: the terminal-intent collision (OPERATION_INTENT_TERMINAL_COLLISION), the REPLACE successor identity built from the predecessor id, schema-job cohort attachment by (job, node) intent id, ReplicaCleanupTombstoneOwner.isCleanupOperationTerminal, queryTerminalFailedCreateCleanupOperations, message-group membership debt and ACTIVE storage reservations. Deletes are guarded and go through the owner gateway in batches paced under the cache-tombstone bound. Deterministic tests cover a retry after retirement, cleanup release after retirement, tombstone-cap pacing and a joiner hydrating mid-batch; the lab proof is three formations and a churn soak. Size L. Not sealable before the owner rules what a deterministic-intent retry answers once its earlier terminal row has been retired.

constraints.statement: No row deletion lands before the fresh-formation scenario holds three consecutive lab passes and CDC delivery stages 1-3 (solve/epics/operation-integrity-and-reliable-formation/cdc-delivery-design-note-2026-11-11.md) have landed.
Retention never changes what a retry answers without an explicit owner ruling recorded in this log before the quest is sealed.
One retention owner per table and one deletion path (R01, R11). Retention rides an existing reconcile trigger; it adds no timer.

A row is deleted only when it is terminal AND past its per-table horizon AND proven unreferenced by every dependency listed for its table (the seven named in the statement). Age and terminal status alone never authorize a delete.

Deletes are guarded and idempotent (R14) and run in bounded batches paced under the cache-tombstone bound (30 s TTL, 1024 tombstones per table), at background priority, so that load slows retention and never breaks correctness (R12).

A propagated table is never expired by time inside apply: that bypasses CDC and leaves every cache stale. Its rows are deleted through the owner gateway so each delete is a replicated mutation with its CDC obligation.
Retention removes whole unreferenced rows. It never shortens steps_history: entry 0 is the metadata channel and the history is a strictly-extending transition mirror.

A late upsert after tombstone expiry can resurrect a cache row until the next authoritative absence sweep. The quest proves a retired row does not come back as a decision input: either the pacing keeps tombstones alive past every in-flight delivery, or the resurrected row is shown to be harmless to each listed dependency.
Join, rejoin, rebalance and partitioning changes are assumed coupled: the proof includes a joiner hydrating while a batch runs and a churn soak, not only a quiet cluster.

A table moves out of class unbounded in solve/epics/system-table-retention/table-lifetimes.json only in the change that lands its retention owner, and the retained entry names that owner as file:symbol. The declaration is never edited to lower the epic metric ahead of the code.
The src/ changes land only behind an approving verification newer than the last attempt.
